newsitem.title: PERU: Freed Peru hostages say they are threatened-report.
newsitem.headline: Freed Peru hostages say they are threatened-report.

text.p: Former hostages freed by Marxist rebels from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima said they were under surveillance and have received death threats, a local newspaper said on Tuesday.

"I received an anonymous call warning me to keep quiet about my ideas that negotiation should be used to achieve releases from the Japanese residence," former Economy Minister Gustavo Saberbein, a freed hostage, was quoted as saying by opposition daily La Republica.

Javier Diez Canseco, an opposition party legislator, said that since his release when the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels proposed him as a mediator in the crisis his house has been watched constantly and he has been followed when he leaves his home, the newspaper reported.
A third freed hostage, economist Alejandro Toledo, said his telephone had been tapped.

All three said they believed Peru's intelligence service was carrying out the surveillance and suspected them of collaboration with the MRTA guerrillas, who stormed the residence on Dec. 17, taking more than 500 hostages.

"The intelligence service's main activity is to investigate the country's enemies but they have the mistaken aim of trying to follow those people who have different beliefs (than) the government instead of investigating those groups who take up arms," Saberbein said.
The rebels have released some 430 hostages but still hold 74, including top government and security force officials, two foreign ambassadors and about two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
